named_events.loss_description: The level of insured global catastrophe in 2024 has totalled ~$140bn according to Munich Re's research division. This is the fifth most costly year since 1980. $47bn of this was due to US hurricane, although through a number of events rather than one single large event.

named_events.event_name: International wind, flood, hail and earthquake losses
named_events.loss_description: Material wind, flood, hail and earthquake losses internationally, (excluding the US), have also given rise to a material level of insured losses in 2024.
The Marine and Specialty portfolio continued to also see some positive rate change post the Baltimore bridge collision.

On the 7 January 2025, a series of devastating wildfires started in Los Angeles, which quickly spiralled out of control due to drought conditions and strong winds. The event is expected to trigger material losses to Syndicate 6117 and considering the uncertainty involved, a reliable estimate of the associated outflows cannot be made. However, this is not expected to impact the going concern of Syndicate 6117. As the event occurred after the balance sheet date, the technical provisions included in these financial statements do not contain any estimates in relation to the wildfires.
